column2: Clean water is a promise. Do not sell her a promise you cannot keep.
The spring does not ask who can afford a drink. The filter supplier unfortunately does.
He trusts a service record more than a blessing.
We repaired a cistern without a ceremony. I think the spring will forgive us.
She checks every sample, including the ones donated for free.
The kitchens fed three streets last night. We will need to refill every shelf.
His route passes through neighborhoods the regular suppliers avoid.
A pilgrim brought a map with seven wells. We have found two and a very convincing puddle.
Some of the oldest purification instructions still work best.
The children voted to name our newest pump. It is now called Sir Drips.
He measures a donation by how many people it feeds.
We count clean cups as carefully as donations. Both disappear faster than expected.
